## Cleaning IMPC_Param_Desc

#ParameterID is our primary key, therefore it should have no duplicates

```{r}

length(unique(impc_param_desc$parameterId)) # number of unique parameter ID values
```

```{r}
cat("Unique Orig Parameter ID values:\n")

impc_param_desc[duplicated(impc_param_clean$impcParameterOrigId), ] #display duplicates of orig paramID
```

```{r}
impc_param_desc[duplicated(impc_param_desc), ] #display duplicate rows
impc_param_desc[duplicated(impc_param_desc$parameterId), ] #display duplicates of paramID


# remove whitespaces from all chr columns
library(dplyr)

impc_param_clean <- impc_param_desc %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), trimws))

impc_param_clean <- impc_param_clean[!duplicated(impc_param_clean$parameterId), ] #remove duplicates of paramID

impc_param_clean[duplicated(impc_param_clean$parameterId), ]

glimpse(impc_param_clean)

cat("\n")

summary(impc_param_clean)
```

### Saving the IMPC Param File

```{r}

write_csv(impc_param_clean, "Clean Files/impc_param_clean.csv")
```

## Batch import data files

```{r}
files <- list.files("data", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)

read_one <- function(f) {
  read_csv(f, col_names = c("field", "value"),
           col_types = "cc", trim_ws = TRUE, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(field = tolower(field)) %>%   #lower case column names since there is inconsistency
    pivot_wider(names_from = field, values_from = value)
}

raw <- map_dfr(files, read_one)

results <- raw %>%
  mutate(pvalue = as.numeric(pvalue))
```

```{r}
glimpse(results)
cat("\n")
summary(results)
```

## Data Conversion

**#Check whether values outside what is listed should be converted or excluded**

```{r}
unique(raw$mouse_strain) # Values are C57BL; B6J; C3H; 129SV
```

```{r}
results %>%
  filter(str_detect(results$mouse_strain, "C3H")) # Check for the above values in mouse_strain
```

NB: There is no mouse strain with value 'C3H'

```{r}
strain_values <- c("C57BL", "B6J", "C3H", "129SV")

results %>%
  filter(!mouse_strain %in% strain_values) %>%  # count each no. values outside the list
  count(mouse_strain, sort = TRUE)
```

Keeping only values in SOP

```{r}
permissible_values <- results %>%
  filter(mouse_strain %in% strain_values)
```

**#Clean mouse_life_stage column. Standardize the casing.**

```{r}
unique(results$mouse_life_stage)  # Values are E12.5; E15.5; E18.5; E9.5; Early adult; Late adult; Middle aged adult


permissible_values <- permissible_values %>%
  mutate(mouse_life_stage = trimws(str_to_title(mouse_life_stage))) # Sentence case values in 'mouse_life_stage' column

unique(permissible_values$mouse_life_stage) 


permissible_values$mouse_life_stage[permissible_values$mouse_life_stage == "Na"] <- NA # Set 'Na' values to NA
```

```{r}

sum(is.na(permissible_values$mouse_life_stage)) # count NA mouse_life_stage values
permissible_values %>% filter(is.na(mouse_life_stage)) # show the above values
```

**Check for duplicate ID values and clean**

```{r}
permissible_values[duplicated(permissible_values), ] #display duplicate rows

permissible_values[duplicated(permissible_values$analysis_id), ] #display duplicates of analysis_id

permissible_values[duplicated(permissible_values$gene_accession_id), ] #display duplicates of gene_accession_id

permissible_values[duplicated(permissible_values$parameter_id), ] #display duplicates of parameter_id
```

**Check for duplicates in gene symbol, since there duplicates in gene_accession_id**

```{r}

#display duplicates of gene_symbol
permissible_values[duplicated(permissible_values$gene_symbol), ] 


# display the number of gene symbols each gene_accession_id has
permissible_values %>% distinct(gene_accession_id, gene_symbol) %>%  
  count(gene_accession_id) %>% filter(n > 1)
```

NB: From our analysis, the gene symbols are only different because some are capitalised. All the gene_accession IDs say 'MGI', proving they are mouse genes. Hence we convert to title format.

**Standardise casing in Gene_Symbol**

```{r}
# Convert the values in 'gene_symbol' to title format
permissible_values <- permissible_values %>%
  mutate(gene_symbol = trimws(str_to_title(gene_symbol)))
```

**Standardise Gene_Accession_ID and Parameter_ID values**

```{r}
permissible_values <- permissible_values %>%
  mutate(gene_accession_id = trimws(str_to_upper(gene_accession_id)),
         parameter_id = trimws(str_to_upper(parameter_id))
         ) # Upper case the values in 'gene_accession_id' and parameter_id' columns
```

From our analysis, Gene_accession_ID and parameter_ID have duplicates due to inconsistent capitalisation. Hence, we standardise the casing.

**Check if parameter_id has more than one parameter_name**

```{r}
permissible_values %>% distinct(parameter_id, parameter_name) %>%  
  count(parameter_id) %>% filter(n > 1)
```

**Creating a new table with parameterID values from the batch data files and IMPC_param**

```{r}
# Combine paramID values from both tables into one
parameter_clean <- bind_rows(
  permissible_values %>% distinct(parameter_id, parameter_name),
  impc_param_clean %>% distinct(parameter_id = parameterId)) %>%
  
  # group by param ID and keep one ID per grouping 
  group_by(parameter_id) %>%
  summarise(parameter_name = first(na.omit(parameter_name)), .groups = "drop")
```

### Saving results to .csv files

```{r}
# keeping unique sets of gene_accession_id and gene_symbol
gene <- permissible_values %>% distinct(gene_accession_id, gene_symbol)

# Save to .csv
write_csv(gene, "Clean Files/gene_clean.csv")


# Save parameter table to .csv
write_csv(parameter_clean, "Clean Files/parameter_clean.csv")


# each row of analysis_id is already unique
analysis <- permissible_values %>% select(analysis_id, gene_accession_id, parameter_id,
                               mouse_strain, mouse_life_stage, pvalue) 

# Save to .csv
write_csv(analysis, "Clean Files/analysis_clean.csv")

```
